newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macquarie executive faces insider trading trial.
newsitem.headline: Macquarie executive faces insider trading trial.

text.p: High-flying Australian corporate finance advisor Simon Hannes was committed for trial on Tuesday on charges of insider trading over the A$2 billion takeover of TNT Ltd last year.

Hannes, an executive director with Macquarie Bank Ltd, became one of Australia's highest-profile coporate takeover advisors after he orchestrated the 1995 merger of mining giants RTZ Corp Plc and CRA Ltd.

The 37-year-old is now alleged to have used inside information about the October 1996 bid by Dutch postal and telecoms group KPN for TNT when he allegedly posed as a trader known as "Mark Booth" to buy TNT options.
Macquarie Bank advised transport firm TNT on the KPN bid.
"Booth" bought about A$90,000 worth of A$2 options on September 17 and 18 before the surprise A$2.45 a share bid on October 2 and would have made a A$2 million profit.

The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) has said its investigators recovered deleted files from the hard disk on Hannes' personal laptop computer and found papers from his home which they said showed Hannes and Booth were one and the same.
Prosecutors told the St James local court that although Hannes was not working on the TNT account, known as Project Tennis, he found out about it through colleagues.
Hannes is alleged to have asked a fellow Macquarie employee in July 1996 what TNT's shares had been valued at and was told they were valued at between A$2 a share and over A$3 a share.
TNT's shares were trading at about A$1.30 a share at the time.

Evidence tendered in court also showed Hannes used his electronic security key to access Macquarie Corporate Finances offices late at night on three weekends in September even though he was on leave at the time.
Documents on the TNT takeover were freely available in the offices.
Hannes, appearing relaxed and confident in rimless glasses, a dark suit and a spotted tie, told the court he had reserved his defence for a trial expected next year.
His lawyers have previously said Hannes would plead not guilty to related charges that Hannes tried to conceal the transactions need to buy the options.
Hannes appears in court again on Friday to make a plea on the charges.
